Dr. Okafor had delivered hard news before, but the room still felt very small. The family sat in a row along the wall — the mother, two sons, an aunt who had driven overnight — and she pulled her chair close and spoke slowly. The scan showed what they had feared. She didn’t rush to fill the silence afterward. One of the sons looked at the floor; the mother’s hand found his. “What happens now?” she asked at last. Dr. Okafor explained the options in plain words, one at a time, and when she finished she said, “There’s no wrong question.” They asked a great many anyway. By the time she left the room the afternoon had slipped away, and the hallway lights had come on.
